text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the prematurity at 33 weeks and onset of distress within two hours, I suspect Respiratory Distress Syndrome due to surfactant deficiency. I will proceed to evaluate the chest imaging and blood gases to confirm.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-Ray: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs; Arterial_Blood_Gas: pH 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2 50 mmHg (elevated), PaO2 60 mmHg (reduced), HCO3- 24 mEq/L

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a 33-week preterm infant with early-onset respiratory distress, grunting, and retractions is classic for surfactant deficiency. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (NRDS)
